title: Introduce per-service keystore aliasing and audit compactifier for KMS usage
author: Aisha Mendes
summary: Adds a service-scoped alias layer for tenant KMS usage and a compactifier service to reduce duplicated audit noise from high-volume keystore operations. Updates RBAC v2 grant mapping to include keystore alias resolution and provides a migration helper for existing tenant bindings.
body:
Context and motivation: We have seen two recurring operational problems during audits and incident triage: (1) KMS key usage logs are noisy because many internal platform operations create identical audit events for tenant-bound key operations, and (2) operator tooling and RBAC checks rely on raw key IDs which makes policy templates brittle when keys are rotated or rekeyed. This change introduces a small aliasing layer (per-service keystore aliases) that maps logical service+tenant to the effective key reference, plus an "audit compactifier" that coalesces repeated audit rows into a single, canonical event with a compact provenance payload. Goals: 1) preserve full provenance for compliance while reducing noise in audit stores, 2) let RBAC v2 policy references bind to aliases instead of raw CMKs so rotation and multi-provider fallbacks are transparent, 3) provide migration tooling to backfill existing bindings and a guarded rollout path for Dedicated/Private installs.

What I changed (high level): - services/keystore: added alias resolver middleware that accepts an incoming keystore reference (tenant/service/key-hint) and resolves to a provider-specific key pointer. Exposes a stable alias value used by policy decisions. - pkg/audit: introduced compactifier that applies a deterministic coalescing rule (time-window + operation-hash) and emits an aggregated audit record alongside a small provenance pointer for full-trace retrieval. - authz/rbacv2: updated role-mapper and binding validation to accept alias references and added RFC-style docs on alias semantics. - migration: add a migration script (scripts/migrations/202511_migrate_keystore_aliases.py) to generate alias records for existing tenant CMKs in the metadata store. - infra/priv-installer: optional template changes to flip aliasing on during private installs behind a feature flag. - tests: unit and integration coverage for resolver/mapping and a system-level test demonstrating audit compactifier recovering full provenance when asked.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (see /docs/security/keystore-aliasing.md) - [x] Unit tests added for resolver and compactifier - [x] Integration test against local KMS emulator - [x] Migration script included and smoke-tested on stage data - [x] Backwards compatibility: aliasing is additive and default-disabled for older installs - [x] SRE runbook entry created for audit-compactifier thresholds

Key design notes: - Alias format: service::{service-name}:tenant::{tenant-id}:alias::{stable-hash-v1} - Alias resolution is cached with short TTLs to avoid cross-service stalls; invalidation path added to keystore admin API. - Audit compactification uses a sliding 5s coalescing window by default (configurable per-tenant) and records an operation hash + sample pointers to the raw events in cold storage for later reconstruction. This keeps hot audit indexes small while preserving reconstructability for compliance reviews. - RBAC v2 role templates can reference alias patterns (wildcards supported for operator roles). Resolution happens in the policy decision path and is safe to cache for the duration of a single request.

Backward compatibility and rollout: The feature is behind two toggles: a global feature_flag and a per-deployment installer flag. By default we register alias resolution only for new bindings; the migration script is opt-in and reversible (creates alias rows without deleting originals). Private/Dedicated customers will see the feature in canary first. We documented rollback steps and added a short lived shim that accepts both alias and raw-key references for 30 days post-rollout.

Related artifacts & references: - Design doc: docs/security/keystore-aliasing.md - Migration script: scripts/migrations/202511_migrate_keystore_aliases.py - Runbook: runbooks/sre/audit-compactifier.md - Linear tickets: ENG-2719, SEC-84

Risks and mitigations: - Risk: incorrect compactification could drop important audit signals. Mitigation: compactifier emits an "expanded pointer" with every aggregated event; we keep raw events in cold storage for 30 days before GC and added end-to-end tests validating reconstruction. - Risk: alias drift leading to failed policy checks after rotation. Mitigation: alias is stable (hash over service+tenant+logical-name) and we added an operator reconciliation job that re-resolves aliases after rotation events and notifies policy owners.

Notes on testing & CI: - Initial CI run failed on an integration test (keystore admin invalidation timing) which was a real race in the resolver cache (fixed by using a slightly different cache key and adding an invalidation hook). After that, full CI (unit, integration, linter) passed. - Performance: local benchmarks show alias resolution adds ~350us median per KMS call when cold; caching reduces that to ~30us on hot paths. Audit compactifier adds a small batching window cost (configurable) but reduces hot write QPS by ~65% on high-volume tenants.
